![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/47eb2f1073f62129ba2fbf7ae154b9733ff2d5bf09af30053f7b708d7a8d21b0.png)

Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $2\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
2\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/220bd5e2559f7e3ef483b1315d1dd98771cf81d8d181a161b87d8084773259e6.png)

Since there are $4$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =4\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={(\theta +\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta ))|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =[(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))] \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
